input.question: Hypothetically what is the worst thing that could happen if I don't turn on "airplane mode"?
input.ground_truth: Nothing. In 2015 alone, airplanes [carried ~3.441B people](_URL_0_). Most of them have devices with radios (phones, tablets, laptops). Many of them simply forgot to turn it off. There has never been a single malfunction of any sort attributed to a GSM/UMTS/LTE or WiFi radio not turned off. As a side note, FAA does not prohibit cellphone (much less WiFi) operation during flight, see 14 CFR 91.21 (b)(5); FCC and carriers do.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Hypothetically what is the worst thing that could happen if I don't turn on "airplane mode"?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your phone is like a little radio. When you’re on a plane, the pilot says, “Please turn your phone to airplane mode.” That means your phone should not talk to cell towers (the big towers outside that help phones call and text).

If you don’t turn on airplane mode, your phone might try to talk to those towers while flying really fast. That could make the phone get confused, use up its battery really fast, and maybe even bother the airplane’s special radios.

The worst thing that could happen is that your phone might try to call or text so much that it could cause a little problem for the airplane, or your phone might not work right until you land. But usually, nothing super bad happens—just that your phone might get hot or lose battery faster. Pilots ask you to do this to be safe!
